decisions.summary: Mon (and kanmon) in silver handled only by reference: 'The copper rates stay in 0277 (named, not repeated)'; no block gives a mon or kanmon rate a home for the Japanese eras outside 0277's span
decisions.why: Q4 asks 'mon (and kanmon), monme, ryo and bu in Japan by decade', and the request's own canon line says '0277 has Osaka 1787-1859 and Edo 1781-1842'. Against the ten Japanese eras of D2, that leaves osaka-1620, osaka-1700, kyoto-1745 and most of osaka-1780 (before 1781) and edo-1860 (after 1859) with no mon-to-silver rate written anywhere: D3 gives ryo and bu an explicit pre-1787 chronology but gives mon none, D2 prices goods not coins, and D7's per-era 'coins in grams of silver' column has no record source for mon in those eras. Purpose test: the GM's own example amount, the Takamiya-Toriimoto fares of 40/27/20 mon, is re-marked by D5 to osaka-1620 (as are the 1611/1658 post-station fees in mon), and converting a mon amount at osaka-1620 needs exactly the 1620-1650 mon rate this plan does not write; the 1766 1/66 monme and the 1700 legal rate are a single point and a legal rate, where Q4 asks the market rate where it moved. 'Named, not repeated' is a placement rule for rates 0277 holds, not an impossibility for the rates it lacks, and nothing in the request implies excluding them. Fix (one sentence in D3): state where mon/kanmon in silver lives for each Japanese era outside 0277's 1781-1859 span (written into C or 0277, the market rate where it left the legal one) or that it is recorded SILENT with the search named; if 0277 already holds those eras, the block can say so by name and this clears.

decisions.summary: Every Chinese amount (0288/0289 and all others, in taels, cash, dollars) is passed over in backfill.md until gm-assistant's table carries Chinese coin keys; T05 asks for those keys on #13; 'once it does, the amounts are marked as the Japanese ones were'.
decisions.why: FR-003 marks every amount whose era this feature defines, and gm-assistant confirmed all thirteen ids, Chinese included, with 'Go ahead with #14's marking on these ids'. The block's reason bundles two gates. (a) gm-assistant's table carrying the eras: not what distinguishes Chinese from Japanese, since the new Japanese eras are not in the table either and are marked anyway against the awaiting list. (b) The Chinese coin key names: these are gm-assistant's to name, and declining to invent them is right. But a name that can be had by asking is not an impossibility, and the plan makes it unobtainable by its own ordering: T05 (the ask) runs 'after ... the marks (T06)', and T07 lands 'once T01-T06 are ticked', so no task consumes the answer before landing and 'once it does, the amounts are marked' has no carrier. As written the whole Chinese half of FR-003 ships unmarked behind a question in the closing comment - a narrowing framed as an open question. (The dispatch says the keys 'are asked on #13'; the thread as of 2026-10-24 carries no such ask, and the block says T05 will ask.) Fix: ask gm-assistant for the Chinese coin keys on #13 BEFORE s5, and make T06's done-measure name either the Chinese amounts marked under the keys gm-assistant gave, or a deferral gm-assistant has confirmed on #13 - not one the plan assumes.

decisions.summary: Alternative exit: if gm-assistant confirms a deferral on #13, each Chinese question is passed over in backfill.md with that reason and the comment's URL.
decisions.why: Round 2 blocked a deferral the session assumed. Here the session assumes nothing: the default path is full marking, and the narrower exit opens only on the requester's own words on #13, which would themselves be the requester relaxing its request, not a session carving out a case. The dependency is real, not convenience: coin keys are keys in gm-assistant's table, which the diagram side said on #13 it will not write into, and a mark under an unconfirmed key converts nothing, so the purpose (a hovered amount converts at its era's prices) cannot be met by guessing keys. Done line requires either branch to be evidenced (confirmed keys and marks, or a cited confirmed deferral).
